scope: General outfitter and guide license, the separate whitewater license, the 42-company portal, New River Gorge fishing observations, and reuse terms. Personal names and contact lines are omitted.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
sources.field_scope: General outfitter and guide license. Fee $10 by check or money order to DNR Law Enforcement. The applicant sends a signed and notarized application, an original surety bond, a West Virginia business license, proof of liability insurance, an insurance and bond form, and a first aid card. A Natural Resources Police officer inspects equipment after the Attorney General approves the bond. The license certificate is mailed. Whitewater-zone user reporting is described as a separate duty: $0.70 per user on the Gauley and $0.35 per user on other rivers, with login credentials issued by Law Enforcement. A National Forest permit requires this license first. A motorboat guide born after December 31, 1986 needs a boater-education certificate unless the guide holds a federal commercial boater operator license. Boat-livery orientation is a separate duty under the posted boating code. District telephones, the Law Enforcement telephone, the mail street, and the wildlife mailbox were not copied.
sources.bulk: No holder list on this page. It links the application packet and the posted rule and code PDFs.
sources.attribution: Cite WVDNR and the page. The site footer is copyright 2026.
sources.request_process: Mail the packet to the Law Enforcement Section. No one was contacted.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources, Law Enforcement

Section 5 asks for services, areas, and whitewater zones. The packet also copies the posted code and the 2018 rule. A Social Security number was not on the form pages that were read.
sources.bulk: Blank application. Not an issued-license file.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Secretary of State
sources.field_scope: Final Word file for the active Series 11, last saved April 19, 2024. Filing date and effective date April 19, 2024. Sunset August 1, 2029. Authority line inside the file is W. Va. Code §§20-1-7(31) and 20-2-23, which does not match the index line. An outfitter provides boats or guide services for profit for hunting, fishing, or taking expeditions. The applicant may elect the outfitter or guide designation. Licenses expire December 31 of the year of issue. Bond is $1,000. Liability minimums are $300,000 bodily injury per occurrence and $25,000 property damage. Proof is due by February 15 each year. First aid is required for the person conducting the service. Boats must be kept in safe operable condition. Whitewater study fees in this text are $0.35 per customer on the Cheat, New, Shenandoah, and Tygart study zones and $0.70 on the Gauley. The companion final PDF is a scanned image and returned no text. Staff names in the Word metadata were not copied.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
sources.field_scope: Agency copy of §20-2-23. PDF created November 8, 2019. Defines outfitter to include a person who, for profit, provides boats or guide services for fishing or other taking expeditions. An occasional favor rental is outside the definition. The live code site did not connect on this check.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
sources.field_scope: Agency copy of §20-2-24. Created November 8, 2019. The licensee is a financially responsible United States citizen and must possess the equipment that is advertised. The director investigates qualifications before issuing a license.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
sources.field_scope: Agency copy of §20-2-25. Created November 8, 2019. The application states name, address, property to be used, area to be served, citizenship, and age. Three resident real-property owners of the applicant's county sign it. A national-forest license also needs the forest supervisor's site designation and permit.
sources.attribution: Cite W. Va. Code §20-2-25 as posted by WVDNR.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
sources.field_scope: Agency copy of §20-2-26. Created November 8, 2019. Fee $10. The license is for the calendar year designated on it. Surety bond $1,000 for the life of the license, approved as to form by the Attorney General. The director may revoke the license.
sources.attribution: Cite W. Va. Code §20-2-26 as posted by WVDNR.

sources.publisher: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
sources.field_scope: A separate Whitewater Outfitter and Guide License. Structured data was published June 11, 2021, and modified June 9, 2025. Non-refundable application fee $250 with a letter of intent. Applications submitted by March 15 are considered for a license effective January 1 of the following calendar year. The page prints a commission deadline of September 31. After approval the annual license fee is $500 per license. Before operation the licensee submits a $1,000 outfitter and guide surety bond, commercial general liability insurance, and passes an equipment and location inspection that includes CPR and first aid. The mail street was not copied. The page links an insurance-and-bond PDF that was not opened.
sources.attribution: Cite the how-to page and the June 9, 2025 modification date.
